metadata.title: Dokistry - Manage your self-hosted Docker registries
metadata.description: Monitor and manage self-hosted Docker registries, images, and users from a single modern interface.

hero.title: Monitor Docker registries
hero.description: A single modern interface to monitor and manage your self-hosted Docker registries, images, and users.

features.title: Everything You Need
features.subtitle: Comprehensive Docker registry management in one clean interface

imageInspection.title: Image Inspection
imageInspection.description: View detailed information about images and tag sizes. Monitor disk usage across your registries.

tagInspection.title: Tag Inspection
tagInspection.description: Inspect and analyze tags on each registry. Get comprehensive metadata at a glance.

tagsDeletion.title: Tags Deletion
tagsDeletion.description: Delete tags directly from the interface. Clean up unused resources efficiently.

multiRegistry.title: Multi-Registry
multiRegistry.description: Manage multiple registries from one instance. Switch between registries effortlessly.

userManagement.title: User Management
userManagement.description: Add and manage users with admin privileges. Control access to your registries securely.

easyDeployment.title: Easy Deployment
easyDeployment.description: Deployable with one click via Dokploy or via Docker Compose. Quick and simple installation.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Dokistry

isItFree.question: Is Dokistry free?
isItFree.answer: Yes, Dokistry is completely free and open source. It is distributed under the MIT license, which means you can use, modify, and distribute it freely, even for commercial projects.

howToInstall.question: How to install Dokistry?
howToInstall.answer: Dokistry can be easily deployed via Docker Compose. It is also available with one click on Dokploy, which allows for an even simpler and faster deployment.

supportedRegistries.question: Which Docker registries are supported?
supportedRegistries.answer: For now, Dokistry only supports the Docker Registry v2 API. All self-hosted Docker registries that use this API are supported. For now, it does not support Harbor, Nexus Repository and other APIs, but this can be implemented based on community needs.

userManagement.question: Can I create users and manage access?
userManagement.answer: Yes, Dokistry allows you to create and manage users. There are two roles: administrator and basic member. Administrators can manage registries and users, while basic members cannot manage registries or users.

howToContribute.question: How can I contribute to the project?
howToContribute.answer: There is a contribution guide on the GitHub repository. You can contribute by developing new features, improving documentation, reporting bugs, proposing improvements, or translating the interface.

reportBug.question: Where can I report a bug or suggest a feature?
reportBug.answer: You can report bugs or suggest new features via our issue system on GitHub. Please check first if the problem or feature has not already been reported before creating a new issue.

isItActive.question: Is the project still actively developed?
isItActive.answer: Yes, Dokistry is an active project in continuous development. We regularly publish updates, improvements, and new features. You can follow our progress on GitHub and see the latest versions in the releases.
